title: Abhyankar height bound for valuations of finitely generated fields
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] finitely generated as a field over its prime subfield $F$ (the smallest subfield of $K$, isomorphic to $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$). Let $d=\operatorname{trdeg}_F K$, the finite size of a transcendence basis, i.e. a maximal algebraically independent subset of $K$ over $F$. For every valuation ring $A\subseteq K$ with fraction field $K$, meaning that for each $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ belongs to $A$, every strictly increasing chain of prime ideals of $A$ has length at most $d+1$. Equivalently the height of $A$ is at most $d+1$, with length counting strict inclusions.

source.place: §2.1, Corollary 2.1.3(i), p. 8, specialized to fields finitely generated over their prime field; its proof uses Lemma 2.1.2 (Abhyankar inequality).

proof.text: Because K is finitely generated over its prime subfield F, a finite transcendence basis exists and its cardinality is the stated finite integer d. Fix the valuation ring A and write Gamma_K for its value group, A_F=A\cap F for the induced valuation ring on F, and kappa_K=A/m_A and kappa_F=A_F/m_{A_F} for the residue fields.

source.place: §2.1, setup preceding Lemma 2.1.2; local document copy unavailable

proof.text: Apply the relative Abhyankar inequality [lem-trf-abhyankar-inequality] to F\subseteq K and A. It gives rrk(Gamma_K/Gamma_F)+trdeg_{kappa_F}(kappa_K)\le d. Since the residue transcendence degree is nonnegative, rrk(Gamma_K/Gamma_F)\le d.

source.place: §2.1, Lemma 2.1.2 (relative form); local document copy unavailable

proof.text: The map $\Gamma_F\to\Gamma_K$ is injective, because $A_F^\times=A^\times\cap F^\times$ (if $x,x^{-1}\in A$ with $x\in F$, both lie in $A_F$). Tensoring the short exact sequence $0\to\Gamma_F\to\Gamma_K\to\Gamma_K/\Gamma_F\to0$ with the flat $\mathbf Z$-module $\mathbf Q$ keeps it exact, so $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_K)=\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_F)+\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_K/\Gamma_F)$. By [lem-trf-prime-field-valuation-rank], applied to the valuation ring $A_F$ of the prime field $F$, $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_F)\le1$; with the bound $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_K/\Gamma_F)\le d$ of Step 2 from [lem-trf-abhyankar-inequality], $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_K)\le d+1$.

source.place: §2.1, Lemma 2.1.2 and prime-field valuation discussion; local document copy unavailable

proof.text: For any finite strictly increasing chain of prime ideals of A with n strict inclusions, [lem-trf-valuation-height-rank] gives n\le rrk(Gamma_K). Combining this with Step 3 yields n\le d+1. Since the chain was arbitrary, every chain has length at most d+1, which is the asserted height bound.

proof_origin.place: §2.1, Lemma 2.1.2 and Corollary 2.1.3(i); the local document copy is unavailable

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-2dfd6b23f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The mathematics is correct; I read it all. The item says a valuation ring of a field K finitely generated over its prime field has height at most trdeg+1. That matches how lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement uses it in step 8, and small cases agree (F_p; Q with Z_(p), height 1 = d+1; Q(x) with rank-2 valuations, height 2). Steps: 2 applies the relative Abhyankar inequality to get rrk(Gamma_K/Gamma_F) <= d. 3 needs Gamma_F -> Gamma_K injective, since A_F^x = A^x cap F^x, and tensoring with Q exact; then the prime-field node gives rrk(Gamma_F) <= 1, so rrk(Gamma_K) <= d+1. 4 uses height <= rrk. The three new nodes are true standard results, tested on small cases: the relative inequality on Q(x) with the Gauss and x-adic valuations, and Q with Z_(p) (the counterexample to the old absolute form); valuations of Q and F_p; Z_(p), lexicographic Z^2, and value group Q+Q*sqrt2. They are strictly smaller than the item and duplicate no existing node (rg over dag/nodes; the sbc Abhyankar nodes are the tame-ramification lemma; lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height and lem-trf-valuation-value-group-torsion state different things). Everything is in the same unit, so there are no tool_uses. The Temkin 0707.3953 PDF is not in literature/ and Stacks has no Abhyankar inequality, so I could not check §2.1 / Cor 2.1.3(i) against the text: proof_origin is agent with WANTED, and the mathematics agrees with Bourbaki AC VI §10.3. FIX, in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula: (B4) the three new statements were plain text, now TeX; (B3) 'valuation ring' and m_A were used without a definition, now defined inline, and the wrong phrase 'ordered-group quotient' became 'quotient abelian group'; item step 3 now writes out the injectivity and the flatness of Q. No statement's meaning changed and no node is dropped.; 4 file(s) fixed by the reviewer

lean.statement: theorem abhyankar_finite_type_field_height (F : Type u) (K : Type v) [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] (hprime : (⊥ : Subfield K) = (algebraMap F K).fieldRange) (hfg : (⊤ : IntermediateField F K).FG) (d : ℕ) (hd : Algebra.trdeg F K = d) : ∀ (A : ValuationSubring K) (n : ℕ) (p : Fin (n + 1) → PrimeSpectrum A), StrictMono p → n ≤ d + 1
